sources.quote: The PHP security team released emergency security patches for two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell.
Two critical RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), collectively tracked as PHP2Shell, have been successfully exploited in the wild.

claims.statement: PHP disclosed two critical remote-code-execution vulnerabilities, tracked as PHP2Shell.

sources.quote: experts say bad actors could exploit vulnerability in language used by 70% of sites
warns that hackers have figured out a way to exploit the popular PHP software, used in 70% of the web's software.

claims.statement: The flaws could affect roughly 70% of the web's sites, which run on PHP.

sources.quote: Websites taken down across Europe ahead of critical cyber-security update
Websites down as precaution as exploits have already been published
Government websites in the EU and Canada taken offline over PHP vulnerability

claims.statement: Governments and companies took websites offline as a precaution while patching.

sources.quote: Amazon Web Services logged attempts to leverage the internet-melting PHP2Shell bugs four days ago.
Security researchers at Amazon Threat Intelligence say attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell flaws four days before security patches were released on Wednesday.

claims.statement: Amazon found attackers probing the flaws days before patches were made public.

sources.quote: The PHP Meltdown Shows How AI Makes Bugs More Exploitable
AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.

claims.statement: AI tools were involved both in uncovering the vulnerabilities and in attackers later exploiting them.

sources.quote: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to its catalog of actively exploited security flaws and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by Thursday.
Both critical PHP flaws land on the agency's exploited list as infosec pros confirm hackers are getting working shells

claims.statement: CISA added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to its known-exploited catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch.

sources.quote: PHP armageddon: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet

claims.statement: OpenAI and Google's security team Wiz were credited with finding the vulnerabilities.

sources.quote: OpenAI says researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol uncovered two critical PHP vulnerabilities with severity scores of 9.2 and demonstrated working exploits, after which the company coordinated fixes.

claims.statement: OpenAI said its GPT-5.6 Sol model specifically uncovered the flaws, which had severity scores of 9.2.

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets differ on who gets credit for discovering the flaws: one credits OpenAI and Google's Wiz jointly, another attributes it solely to OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model.

quotes.quote: OpenAI, Google's Wiz find ancient holes
OpenAI says researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol uncovered two critical PHP vulnerabilities

discrepancies.explanation: Most coverage describes exactly two critical PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, but one outlet later reported a third bug.

quotes.quote: two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) tracked collectively as PHP2Shell
There's a third PHP2Shell bug, but it won't get an emergency fix

analysis.headline: Two critical PHP flaws disrupt the web; a third bug later emerges
analysis.summary: PHP disclosed two critical remote-code-execution flaws, dubbed PHP2Shell, prompting website shutdowns worldwide, AWS-logged pre-disclosure attacks, and eventual CISA confirmation of active exploitation; outlets differ on who found the bugs and whether a later third flaw changes the count.
